NORTHTEK OBSERVATORY -- VISUAL AND SPECTROSCOPIC LOG (SYNTHETIC, ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY). Session 14, night of March 22, instrument 0.6-meter reflector, seeing 2.1 arcsec.

Entry 01. Sirius A was acquired at right ascension 06:45:09 and held in the crosshairs for photometry. The apparent magnitude of Sirius A was logged at -1.46, the brightest point source of the session.

Entry 02. Betelgeuse rose late and was tracked to declination +07:24:25. The apparent magnitude of Betelgeuse was recorded at 0.50, consistent with its known slow variability.

Entry 03. Proxima Centauri required the longest exposure of the night given its faintness. The distance to Proxima Centauri was confirmed at 4.24 light years from the parallax cross-check. The spectral type of Proxima Centauri was classified as M5.5V from the reduced spectrum.

Entry 04. Vega was centered at right ascension 18:36:56 for calibration purposes. The distance to Vega was logged at 7.68 parsecs, matching the calibration catalog.

Entry 05. The Andromeda Galaxy filled the wide-field frame entirely. The distance to the Andromeda Galaxy was recorded at 2500000 light years, per the reduction pipeline. The redshift of the Andromeda Galaxy was measured at -0.001001, one of the few blueshifted targets of the survey.

Entry 06. Polaris was tracked to declination +89:15:51 for the pole alignment check. The apparent magnitude of Polaris was recorded at 1.98, dimmer than expected under thin cirrus.

Entry 07. Messier 87 was captured in the deep-sky queue. The redshift of Messier 87 was measured at 0.00436. The distance to Messier 87 was logged at 53500000 light years, consistent with the Virgo Cluster distance ladder.

Entry 08. Kepler-186f data was pulled from the archive for cross-reference. The orbital period of Kepler-186f was logged at 129.9 days. The distance to Kepler-186f was recorded at 582 light years from the archived parallax solution.

End of session 14 log.
